Clinical progression involves four stages, with severe outcomes including spasticity, coma, and vegetative states. Survival rates remain below fifty percent two years post-diagnosis, and current treatments are largely ineffective. The article underscores the importance of universal measles vaccination as the only validated defense against this neurological complication. title: Schuylkill County schools preparing for possible measles cases in students

Four measles-attributed deaths have occurred since late August, marking the first in 35 years. While the CDC has not included these deaths in its national count, state officials emphasize the importance of vaccination, noting that over 93% of students are fully vaccinated. School administrators have established procedures for responding to suspected cases, including isolating symptomatic students and coordinating with the state Department of Health. School nurses are trained to identify symptoms, isolate students, and notify public health officials. The state has also published an online tool for parents to access school-level vaccination data and provided guidance to healthcare providers on identifying and treating measles cases. Officials urge parents to ensure their children’s MMR vaccinations are up to date and to keep sick children home, as measles is highly contagious and can spread before symptoms appear.

These deaths were confirmed by independent coroners and state health officials. The federal government acknowledged one measles death on the CDC website, though details remain limited. The CDC is working on a standardized case definition for measles deaths. The outbreak has prompted increased vaccination efforts, with over 38,000 doses administered in the first three weeks of September 2026. The outbreak has raised concerns about vaccination rates, particularly among the Amish community, where religious objections to the MMR vaccine have been cited as a factor.
